clue.text: Copper and marble made into light stand

indicators.note: raw materials made into something are reshaped, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman turns copper and marble into a lamp base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a joining word but its three letters belong in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabrum is a branched holder for several candles, an ornamental support for lighting.

clue.text: What a wizard at bridge is good at?

definitions.text: What a wizard at bridge is good at?

blocks.clueFragment: What a wizard at bridge is good at?
blocks.note: surface reading: an expert card player skilled at winning rounds of bridge
setter's reading: a wizard is a magician, whose speciality is sleight of hand, while bridge supplies the card-game sense of winning rounds

explanation.walkthrough: A 'wizard at bridge' sounds like a card expert, but a real wizard performs magic; the rounds won in bridge are called tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Magicians perform illusions, and the rounds of a bridge hand are called tricks, so both senses meet in the phrase.

clue.text: Detected one's errant daughter

indicators.note: errant means straying from the proper course, so the letters wander out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent tracks down their wayward daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose something out is to sniff it out or discover it, so nosed works as a past tense for found.

clue.text: Country where a note is forged

indicators.note: a forged item is faked or hammered into new shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation notorious for counterfeit banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state in northern Europe, bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Perhaps this killer flew off the handle

definitions.text: Perhaps this killer flew off the handle

blocks.clueFragment: Perhaps this killer flew off the handle
blocks.note: surface reading: a murderer who lost their temper
setter's reading: literally detached from its shaft, as the blade of a chopping tool might, and that blade is the killing part

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flew off the handle' is the idiom for losing one's temper, but here it is meant literally of a tool's blade coming loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting part of an axe sits on a wooden shaft and could literally fly loose, and it is the lethal part of the weapon.

clue.text: Copies of recipe with special ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients are things mixed together in cooking, so the word's letters are stirred up

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin 'take' heading prescriptions
taken as written

explanation.surface: Duplicates of a cooking recipe that calls for unusual components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' feels like a cookery word but only contributes its abbreviation, as on a doctor's prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Replicas are exact reproductions or duplicates of an original object, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Shows noted for happy endings

blocks.note: surface reading: productions famous for ending well
setter's reading: noted means full of musical notes, and happy endings mark the lighter theatrical genre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' reads as 'famous' but means having musical notes; shows with songs and cheerful conclusions are the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: These stage productions combine songs with light-hearted plots that conclude happily, unlike tragedies.

clue.text: Tampico almost devastated by blow

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the place name is dropped
something devastated is wrecked and thrown into disorder, so the remaining letters are scrambled

blocks.note: Tampico is a port city in Mexico, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Mexican port is laid waste by a hurricane's strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a forceful collision or striking, just as a blow is a hard hit.

clue.text: Birds which raise their young?

blocks.note: surface reading: species of bird that rear their chicks
setter's reading: raise means lift, as building-site machines do, which share their name with long-necked wading birds

explanation.walkthrough: All birds raise young in the rearing sense; the question mark hints that these birds share a name with lifting machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranes are tall wading birds, and the same word names hoisting machines that lift heavy loads.

clue.text: Patched denim and shirt-tail indicate an intellectual's habit

indicators.note: patched cloth is cut up and sewn back together, so the letters are rearranged
the tail of a garment is its hanging edge, read loosely here as taking the extreme letters of the word it follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the end letters of shirt

explanation.surface: Mended jeans and a dangling shirt-tail mark the dress habits of an absent-minded academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses shirt-tail loosely for the letters at the edges of shirt; habit here means a way of thinking, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a habitual way of thinking or settled attitude, the mental habit of a thinker.

clue.text: Former model who reveals all

blocks.note: ex- means former
a model poses, so is a poser

explanation.surface: A one-time artist's model who strips completely.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposer is someone who uncovers or lays bare, so one who discloses everything.

clue.text: Plenty of tricks

blocks.note: surface reading: a large supply of deceptions or stunts
setter's reading: tricks are rounds won in card games, and solo whist has a bid to win nine of them carrying a name that also means plenty

explanation.walkthrough: In solo whist, a call to take nine tricks is named with a word meaning a great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful supply, and in solo whist it is the bid to win nine tricks.

clue.text: Peruvian once in prison

blocks.note: taken as written
the can is slang for jail

explanation.surface: A man from Peru who was formerly locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled ancient Peru, so a member of that people was a Peruvian of long ago.

clue.text: Feeble affair lacking gravity

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the abbreviation that follows is removed

blocks.note: a thing is an affair, as in a romantic fling
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A weak romance with no seriousness to it.
explanation.walkthrough: THING loses its G to leave THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin excuse or argument is weak and unconvincing, a flimsy one.

clue.text: They are often folded after a drive

definitions.text: They are often folded after a drive

blocks.clueFragment: They are often folded after a drive
blocks.note: surface reading: things put away after a car journey, such as maps
setter's reading: a whist drive is a social evening of card play, after which the folding furniture is packed away

explanation.walkthrough: A drive suggests motoring, but a whist drive is a British community card evening, played on collapsible furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding tables used for card games are set up for a whist drive and collapsed afterwards.

clue.text: Usual colours

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular answer

blocks.note: first meaning: normal, customary
second meaning: a flag or banner, regimental colours

explanation.walkthrough: A regiment's colours are its flag, which is also called its standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or regular, and a standard is also a military flag or banner.

clue.text: It keeps citizens in the dark

definitions.text: It keeps citizens in the dark

blocks.clueFragment: It keeps citizens in the dark
blocks.note: surface reading: something that keeps people uninformed
setter's reading: keeps means guards, and in the dark means during the hours after sunset

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps in the dark' is the idiom for withholding information, but here it means guarding people at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A night watch is a guard or patrol protecting a town during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Cloudy ring overhead

definitions.note: adjective for a noun answer: a kind of cloud

blocks.note: first meaning: a dark rain cloud
second meaning: a halo above a saint's head

explanation.definitionFit: Nimbus names a grey rain-bearing cloud, and also the luminous halo painted around holy figures.

clue.text: Early development

blocks.note: first meaning: beforehand
second meaning: progress, a step forward

explanation.definitionFit: Advance as a modifier means ahead of time, and as a noun means progress or improvement.

clue.text: For example, escort girl following City

blocks.note: the Ford Escort is an example of a motor vehicle
Di is a short girl's name
ff. is the abbreviation for following pages

explanation.surface: An escort agency girl trailing someone around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escort' suggests a companion, but here it is the Ford model; 'following' looks like a position word yet supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh capital is a large port in south Wales, so the plain word city is a definition by category.

clue.text: Necklace made from jet or cornelian

indicators.note: made from says the result is constructed out of the material that follows, here a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A necklace crafted from black jet or a red semi-precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a rigid neck ring of twisted metal worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Where to take a turn for the better

definitions.text: Where to take a turn for the better

blocks.clueFragment: Where to take a turn for the better
blocks.note: surface reading: a place to start improving
setter's reading: a better is someone placing wagers, who takes a turn at the tables or wheel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn for the better' is the idiom for improvement, but a better here is one who bets, taking a turn at gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling establishment where punters wager on games of chance.

clue.text: Foolish person could be moonraker without rake!

indicators.note: without means minus, so the second word is taken out of the first
could be suggests the leftover letters might become something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; a moonraker is a Wiltshire native, from a tale of yokels raking a pond for the moon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dimwit compared to a moonraker, the Wiltshire yokel of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is a stupid person, an idiot or fool.

clue.text: They check Very lights soundly

indicators.note: soundly means by sound, so what follows is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: Very lights are signal flares; lights can be fires

explanation.walkthrough: Very lights, named after their inventor, are coloured flares fired from a pistol; 'lights' here are fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Verifiers are people who confirm accuracy, inspecting or testing whether something is true.

clue.text: A piece of French bread

blocks.note: surface reading: a slice of baguette
setter's reading: bread is slang for money, and a piece is a coin, so this is a former French coin

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for cash, and a piece is a coin; France used this unit before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency unit of France until replaced by the euro in 2002.

clue.text: Free to take off Albert!

blocks.note: first meaning: release from bonds
second meaning: remove a watch chain, since an albert is a pocket-watch chain named after Prince Albert

explanation.walkthrough: Albert looks like a man's name, but an albert is a watch chain worn across a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain is to release from shackles and also, literally, to remove a chain.

clue.text: European who could make more of her capital

definitions.text: European who could make more of her capital

blocks.clueFragment: European who could make more of her capital
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who could exploit her city better
setter's reading: the letters of the word more rearrange into the name of a famous capital city

explanation.walkthrough: The capital is Rome, whose letters can be rearranged into MORE; its nation's people are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital of Italy, so a native of that country is the European meant.

clue.text: The knock-on results of team consequences

blocks.note: a side is a team
effects are consequences

explanation.surface: The ripple effects of a team's actions.
explanation.definitionFit: Side effects are secondary, usually unwanted outcomes that follow from a main action.
